```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Tempest enrichment adds computations and optional illustration to a completed
STORM report or finalized Co-STORM session. It keeps the incoming product as the
evidence authority and writes a separate, portable report. A calculation does
not become an accepted research claim, and a generated image is not evidence.

This worked example uses the built-in `datasets::CO2` data for chilling
treatment and carbon uptake in *Echinochloa crus-galli*. The numerical analyses
are real R computations. The offline STORM conversation is an authored replay
fixture: it exercises Tempest's public product path without evaluating a live
model, search provider, or the quality of a live model response.

## Read the study design before analyzing

The [R `datasets::CO2` help page](https://www.stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/zCO2.html)
describes 84 rows from 12 plants: six from Quebec and six from Mississippi.
Each plant was measured over seven ambient CO2 concentrations. Half the plants
of each origin are described by the help page as having been chilled overnight.

The original study by Potvin, Lechowicz, and Tardif (1990),
[*The Statistical Analysis of Ecophysiological Response Curves Obtained from
Experiments Involving Repeated Measures*](https://doi.org/10.2307/1938276),
reports that control and chilled plants were paired within each origin before
treatment. Its [Table 1 in the authors' copy](https://biology.mcgill.ca/faculty/potvin/articles/PotvinLech_90.pdf)
gives the pairs and labels the measured concentration levels in µL/L. The R
help labels `conc` in mL/L, so this report flags the unit discrepancy and uses
the original table's µL/L label without converting the dataset values. The
paper's Methods prose gives the first level as 100, while its table and the R
dataset give 95; the worked example follows the tabulated dataset value.

The help page summarizes treatment as chilling overnight; the article's
Methods give the protocol more precisely as 14 hours at 7°C followed by 10
hours of recovery at 20°C. This example reports both descriptions with their
source and does not substitute one for the other.

The article's table numbers map to R's plant IDs as follows:

| Origin | Matched control and chilled plants |
|---|---|
| Quebec | Qn1–Qc3, Qn2–Qc1, Qn3–Qc2 |
| Mississippi | Mn1–Mc3, Mn2–Mc2, Mn3–Mc1 |

The example records those mappings in its analysis output files. Repeated
concentrations are not counted as independent plants.

## What the analyses measure

The first analysis selects the highest value in the dataset's concentration
column. It computes the chilled-minus-control uptake difference within each
pre-specified plant pair, averages those differences within origin, and then
calculates an equal-origin average and an origin-by-treatment interaction. A
seeded percentile bootstrap resamples the three pair differences within each
origin.

The second analysis plots every plant's response curve with the mean curve for
each origin and treatment. It also calculates a trapezoidal area for each
plant across the seven recorded concentrations, then bootstraps the paired
area differences within origin. This area is an integrated descriptive index;
it is not total carbon fixed and does not replace a repeated-measures model.

There are only three matched pairs per origin. The bootstrap intervals are
exploratory and sensitive to individual pairs. These estimates describe this
dataset; they do not establish a general causal effect or support
population-wide generalization. The data figure and both analyses are
descriptive. The example does not reproduce the paper's original model
comparisons.

The executed scripts give the following paired contrasts. The bootstrap
resamples the three matched differences within each origin 20,000 times with
seed `20261114`; intervals are 95% percentile intervals.

| Quantity | Estimate | Bootstrap interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| Highest level, Quebec chilled-minus-control uptake (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | -2.33 | [-5.60, 1.70] |
| Highest level, Mississippi chilled-minus-control uptake (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | -12.87 | [-17.10, -5.90] |
| Highest level, equal-origin average (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | -7.60 | [-10.68, -4.12] |
| Highest-level interaction: Mississippi minus Quebec (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | -10.53 | [-16.70, -3.57] |
| Integrated curve, Quebec chilled-minus-control (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × µL/L) | -3236.6 | [-5445.2, 85.5] |
| Integrated curve, Mississippi chilled-minus-control (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × µL/L) | -10579.1 | [-15307.2, -6075.8] |
| Integrated-curve interaction: Mississippi minus Quebec (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × µL/L) | -7342.5 | [-12263.2, -2421.8] |

The point estimates are more negative in Mississippi for both summaries. The
Quebec intervals include zero; the other displayed intervals do not. With
three pairs per origin, these resampling intervals are descriptive and
unstable, not a substitute for a design-appropriate inferential analysis or a
basis for a population claim.

## Reproduce the offline report

The example folder contains the authored replay, two analysis scripts, the
static plan, source notes, and a generated illustration:

```{r files, eval=FALSE}
example_dir <- system.file("examples", "enriched-research", package = "tempest")
list.files(example_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

Run the driver with a new output directory. It uses the actual
`tempest_enrich_report()` path and checks the result with
`tempest_read_enriched_report()`:

```{r reproduce, eval=FALSE}
Rscript <- file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript")
system2(
  Rscript,
  c(file.path(example_dir, "run-example.R"), "co2-enriched-report")
)
```

The driver creates a valid completed STORM product with `tempest_run()` using
the authored replay chat and local source records. It does not forge a product
object or call the network. The analysis then reads the installed
`datasets::CO2` data. The response-curve task also writes the exact input rows
to `co2-input.csv`; report hashes cover that file, the pair mappings, output
tables, code, plot, original report, and illustration.
The bundle assigns safe names to outputs; each task's `file_map` in
`report.json` maps original filenames to their archived paths.

The `run-example.R` callback copies the bundled generated image into the task
directory. It does not contact an image API, so the example runs offline. The
report labels the image as AI-generated conceptual artwork and provides alt
text; it depicts neither the original apparatus nor a measured outcome.

## Use a deterministic enrichment plan

A plan is a named list with exactly four fields. Every analysis names its
source IDs, question, R code, and assumptions. Every illustration includes a
prompt, caption, and alt text.

```{r plan-shape, eval=FALSE}
list(
  title = "Cold treatment, contrasting responses",
  summary = "Proposed synthesis, not a new verified claim.",
  analyses = list(list(
    id = "high-co2-uptake",
    title = "Paired plant contrast at the highest CO2 concentration",
    question = "What are the within-origin paired uptake contrasts?",
    code = paste(readLines("analysis/high-co2.R"), collapse = "\n"),
    source_ids = source_ids,
    assumptions = c("Use the original study's plant pairs.")
  )),
  illustrations = list(list(
    id = "greenhouse-concept",
    title = "Conceptual greenhouse scene",
    prompt = "Conceptual barnyard grass artwork; no measurements or labels.",
    alt = "Potted grass plants beside a cool greenhouse chamber.",
    caption = "AI-generated conceptual artwork, not evidence."
  ))
)
```

The real plan in `plan.R` contains two analyses and one illustration, within
the configured task budgets. Its `source_ids` come from the completed product's
`tempest_sources(research)$id` table. A supplied plan avoids model-based
planning, which makes this fixture deterministic.

## Callbacks and code execution

`tempest_enrich_report()` accepts injected planner, executor, and image
callbacks. The R executor uses a fresh Deputy `RSession`; it captures text,
warnings, plots, and files created under the task directory. It uses the local
account's R access and is not an operating-system sandbox. Set
`allow_code = TRUE` only when you explicitly trust the code being executed.
The fixture's scripts are authored, bundled R code; model-proposed code needs
review before granting that permission.

```{r callbacks, eval=FALSE}
report <- tempest_enrich_report(
  research,
  output_dir = "co2-enriched-report",
  plan = plan,
  executor = tempest_r_executor(timeout = 120),
  image_generator = local_image_copy_callback,
  allow_code = TRUE,
  max_analyses = 2L,
  max_illustrations = 1L
)
```

The image adapter [tempest_image_generator()] calls the OpenAI Images API when
invoked and reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` at that time. Its callback and report
metadata do not retain the key. An illustration failure does not erase a
successful R analysis, and failed or skipped task results remain visible.

## Keep research evidence separate from derived results

The `research` member returned by `tempest_researcher()` is the canonical
research product. The enriched report preserves its Markdown, source list, and
run identity, then records each analysis status, output, code, and files. The
summary is explicitly a proposed synthesis. Computed values belong to the
reproducible analysis record; they do not change the original claims, publish
accepted knowledge, or prove the original sources correct.

`tempest_read_enriched_report()` verifies that declared files match their
SHA-256 hashes and rejects missing, extra, linked, or altered files:

```{r read-report, eval=FALSE}
checked <- tempest_read_enriched_report(report@path)
checked@status
checked@manifest$files
```

These hashes detect changes within the bundle. They are not a digital
signature or proof of who created it.

## Use the live Researcher workflow

`tempest_researcher()` runs normal STORM research, then enriches the completed
product. Its `...` arguments go to `tempest_run()`; `enrichment` accepts the
same options as `tempest_enrich_report()` except for `x` and `output_dir`.
Without an explicit plan, the configured model proposes a bounded plan from
the report and its sources. The following example saves proposed analysis code
without running it, and enables the live image adapter. It uses credentials and
network access, and is therefore not run while this vignette builds.

```{r live-researcher, eval=FALSE}
result <- tempest_researcher(
  "How does overnight chilling relate to CO2 uptake in Echinochloa crus-galli?",
  output_dir = "live-co2-enriched-report",
  config = tempest_config(),
  max_questions_per_perspective = 2L,
  enrichment = list(
    executor = tempest_r_executor(timeout = 120),
    image_generator = tempest_image_generator(),
    allow_code = FALSE,
    max_analyses = 2L,
    max_illustrations = 1L
  )
)

result$research # Canonical completed research product
result$report   # Separate, validated enriched report
```

For a reproducible live integration, supply a deterministic planner that
chooses source IDs from the returned `sources$id` and uses reviewed local code.
The automatically proposed plan is model output. Inspect `plan.json` and the
saved analysis scripts before supplying a reviewed plan in a new
`tempest_enrich_report()` call with `allow_code = TRUE`.

## A supervised live qualification report

The [hosted reader edition](https://jameshwade.github.io/tempest/live-research/index.html)
links to the evidence briefing, executed analysis, and downloadable outputs.
It was produced from a live research run using `gpt-6.1-sol` for the research
roles, enrichment planning, and an additional reader-synthesis call, and
`gpt-image-2.6-flare` for a conceptual illustration. The executed R analysis
produced two charts and five CSV files; the report also includes the generated
image.

This was a supervised qualification with additional source preparation and
review. The scanned 1990 paper was transcribed with OCR before the final run, a
custom claim extractor was bounded to source-quoted claims, and the proposed
plan and R code were reviewed. The model revised the plan after review, and a
reader-synthesis rounding error was sent back for correction. These steps are
documented with the report. This artifact is not an unattended benchmark or
the expected output of a no-intervention `tempest_researcher()` call.

Its summary uses a different descriptive comparison from the offline paired
replay above. It averages each plant's uptake across all seven concentrations,
then subtracts the nonchilled group mean from the chilled group mean within
each origin: **−10.14** for Mississippi and **−3.58** for Quebec, in µmol m⁻² s⁻¹.
The supplied live outputs do not include the plant-pair mapping, so these are
unpaired plant-group averages, not paired treatment differences or contrasts at
the highest concentration. They describe this small dataset and do not
establish a population-level effect. OCR may contain transcription errors; the
report also leaves the concentration-unit discrepancy unresolved.
